description: Canonical roster test vectors for Family Beacon. Canonical HERE (docs/FamilyBeacon-Testing.md -> Shared test vectors); consumed by beacon-roster and, by checkout at a pinned ref, by Sund's beaconsim. Never vendor a second copy. docs/FamilyBeacon-Roster.md requires these: 'its test vectors must cover the vouch and removal signatures'. Ed25519 is deterministic per RFC 8032, so every signature here must be reproduced byte-for-byte. The signing domains are in bundles.json; a vouch signs family-beacon/vouch/v1\u0000 || canonical_json(payload) and a removal signs family-beacon/removal/v1\u0000 || canonical_json(payload).

vouch_cases.name: canonical-vouch
vouch_cases.note: The only path into a roster. Signed by the INTRODUCER's identity key over subject + epoch; the signature does not cover itself.

vouch_cases.name: vouch-signed-by-the-subject-itself
vouch_cases.note: Only the founding device self-vouches, and only when founding. Otherwise any device holding a channel could admit itself. The signature is valid; the refusal is structural, which is why it is a separate case.

vouch_cases.name: vouch-with-a-tampered-subject-key
vouch_cases.note: The attacker keeps the introducer's signature and swaps identity_pk for one it controls. Because identity_pk is inside the signed payload, this fails verification rather than silently re-keying the subject.

removal_cases.name: canonical-removal
removal_cases.note: A tombstone, irreversible for this device id. Signed by the remover's identity key.

removal_cases.name: removal-with-a-redirected-subject
removal_cases.note: Repointing a valid removal at a different device is the obvious attack on a broadcast tombstone. subject is inside the signed payload, so it fails.

sync_cases.name: canonical-sync-digest
sync_cases.note: The digest is NOT a signature: a sync rides an authenticated session, so the sender is already known, and the digest only lets a receiver whose roster already matches stop immediately. Devices MUST be sorted by device_id — two senders with the same knowledge have to produce the same bytes.

constants.note: Build-time constants, not configuration. Every implementation must agree, because a family whose devices disagree about the cap would admit devices some members refuse.
